title: K-injective descent of comparisons after arbitrary exact functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_0,\mathcal A_1,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex in $\mathcal A_0$ and $\mathcal A_1$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ for which every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. Let $H:\mathcal A_1\to\mathcal A_0$ be additive with an exact additive left adjoint, and let $E_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ ($i=0,1$) be exact additive functors [def-galois-exact-functor, def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Suppose $c:E_0H\xrightarrow{\sim}E_1$ is a specified natural isomorphism. Use the total right derived functor $RH$ with its canonical comparison unit $\gamma_I:Q(HI)\to RH(QI)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and termwise exact derived functors $D(E_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].
There is a unique natural isomorphism $r_c:D(E_0)RH\xrightarrow{\sim}D(E_1)$ satisfying
$$r_{c,QI}\circ D(E_0)(\gamma_I)=Q(c_I)$$
for every K-injective $I$, with the canonical exact-functor localization comparisons understood. For every K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$, its component at $QN$ is $Q(c_I)$ under the resolution identifications of its source with $Q(E_0HI)$ and its target with $Q(E_1I)$. It is independent of the resolution and natural for all derived morphisms, represented by their unique homotopy classes between K-injectives.
Let also $\mathcal A_2$ be an abelian category with such resolutions, $E_2:\mathcal A_2\to\mathcal B$ exact additive, and $J:\mathcal A_2\to\mathcal A_1$, $P:\mathcal A_2\to\mathcal A_0$ additive with exact additive left adjoints. Specify $d:P\xrightarrow{\sim}HJ$, $c':E_1J\xrightarrow{\sim}E_2$ and $b:E_0P\xrightarrow{\sim}E_2$ such that $b=c'\circ(cJ)\circ(E_0d)$. The functors $H,J,P$ preserve K-injectives, and the comparison $\kappa:RP\xrightarrow{\sim}(RH)(RJ)$ normalized on a K-injective $I$ by $Q(d_I)$ is well-defined using $JI$ as the intermediate K-injective. The derived comparisons satisfy
$$r_b=r_{c'}\circ(r_cRJ)\circ(D(E_0)\kappa).$$
If $H=1_{\mathcal A_0}$, $E_1=E_0$ and $c=1$, then $r_c$ is the identity after the canonical comparison $R1\cong1$. All formulas insert canonical functor associators. An additive exact equivalence of abelian categories preserves and reflects K-injectivity and transports K-injective resolutions; the normalized comparisons above agree under such equivalences. The exact functors $E_i$ are not required to preserve K-injectives.

proof.text: Put $F=D(E_0)RH$ and $G=D(E_1)$. The exact-functor factorization identifies $D(E_i)(QM)$ naturally with $Q(E_iM)$ for every complex $M$. The right-derived comparison $\gamma_I$ is invertible when $I$ is K-injective. Thus there are natural identifications $f_I:F(QI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(E_0HI)$, obtained by inverting $D(E_0)(\gamma_I)$ and then using the exact-functor comparison, and $g_I:G(QI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(E_1I)$. Set $t_I=g_I^{-1}Q(c_I)f_I$. These are isomorphisms with the required normalization on K-injectives.

proof.text: For K-injectives $I,I'$ and a homotopy class $h:I\to I'$, naturality of $\gamma$, of the exact-factorization comparisons and of $c$ gives $G(Qh)t_I=t_{I'}F(Qh)$. This calculation applies to homotopy classes: if $u-v=d s+s d$, applying an additive functor $T$ gives $T(u)-T(v)=T(d)T(s)+T(s)T(d)$, so all termwise functors used respect homotopies. Every derived morphism $QI\to QI'$ has a unique such homotopy class by the cited Hom bijection. Consequently this square holds for every derived morphism between K-injective representatives.

proof.text: For each $X\in D(\mathcal A_1)$ choose a complex representing it and a K-injective resolution, giving $e_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_X$. Define $r_X=G(e_X)^{-1}t_{I_X}F(e_X)$. For $a:X\to Y$, the derived morphism $e_Yae_X^{-1}:QI_X\to QI_Y$ is $Q(h)$ for a unique homotopy class $h$, by the Hom bijection. Substituting it into the preceding square and cancelling $F(e_X)$ and $G(e_Y)$ proves $G(a)r_X=r_YF(a)$. Thus the components define a natural isomorphism $r:F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$. Representatives exist because the derived category is a localization and the assumed resolutions exist.

proof.text: The same square with $e_X:X\to QI$ shows that every natural transformation restricting to $t_I$ must have component $G(e_X)^{-1}t_IF(e_X)$ at $X$. In particular our construction restricts to $t_I$ even if the initial choice at $QI$ was a different resolution: apply the square to the derived isomorphism between the two K-injective representatives. This proves uniqueness and independence of all choices. If $a:N\to I$ is any K-injective resolution, take $X=QN$ and $e_X=Q(a)$. Naturality of $\gamma$ identifies $F(Qa)$ with the source resolution identification, and the exact-functor comparison identifies $G(Qa)$ with the target one. The displayed component formula is then exactly $Q(c_I)$ under those identifications.

proof.text: Apply the right-adjoint preservation theorem separately to $H,J,P$, using their specified exact additive left adjoints. They all preserve K-injectives. In particular, if $I\in\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_2)$ is K-injective, then $JI$ is K-injective in $\mathcal A_1$. The right-derived comparisons therefore identify $RP(QI)$ with $Q(PI)$ and $RH(RJ(QI))$ with $Q(HJI)$: for the latter, first use $\gamma^J_I:Q(JI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RJ(QI)$ and then $\gamma^H_{JI}$. These identifications are natural on the homotopy classes between K-injectives.

proof.text: Under these identifications define $k_I:RP(QI)\to RH(RJ(QI))$ by $Q(d_I):Q(PI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(HJI)$. For a homotopy class $h:I\to I'$, naturality of $d$ says $HJ(h)d_I=d_{I'}P(h)$. Hence $k_I$ is natural on K-injectives. For each $X\in D(\mathcal A_2)$ use $e_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_X$ and define $\kappa_X=(RH\,RJ)(e_X)^{-1}k_{I_X}RP(e_X)$. The Hom bijection represents $e_Yae_X^{-1}$ by a homotopy class, so the preceding square gives naturality by cancellation. It also proves independence of $e_X$ and uniqueness with this normalization, exactly as in steps 3-4. Each factor is invertible, giving the asserted natural isomorphism $\kappa$.

proof.text: Evaluate the claimed composition identity at $QI$ for a K-injective $I\in\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_2)$. Step 5 permits $JI$ as the intermediate K-injective. After its comparison identifications, $D(E_0)(\kappa_{QI})$ is $Q(E_0d_I)$, $r_c$ evaluated at $RJ(QI)\cong Q(JI)$ is $Q(c_{JI})$, and $r_{c',QI}$ is $Q(c'_I)$. The latter use of $r_c$ is justified by its naturality at $\gamma^J_I$. The composite is therefore $Q(c'_I)Q(c_{JI})Q(E_0d_I)=Q(b_I)$, by the assumed identity $b=c'\circ(cJ)\circ(E_0d)$. This is the normalization of $r_b$. Every object is isomorphic to such a $QI$, so naturality and cancellation extend equality to every object. The canonical associators merely reparenthesize these same composites.

proof.text: For H=1, consider the canonical natural isomorphism from the identity's termwise complex functor followed by Q to Q. On K-injective complexes, both this comparison and the recorded right-derived unit are invertible. Apply the extension construction of steps 2-4 to obtain e:R1≅1 satisfying the unit equation on K-injectives. For an arbitrary complex N, choose a resolution N→I. Naturality of e, of the unit, and of the identity-complex comparison, followed by cancellation of the invertible Q(N→I), proves the same equation at N. This equation determines e uniquely on K-injectives, hence everywhere by step 4. For exact E and c the left unitor of E, whiskering e by D(E) satisfies the descent normalization: substitute the equation for e and naturality of the exact-factorization comparison, then evaluate the identity-complex comparison degreewise. Uniqueness of normalized descent gives the stated identity formula.

proof.text: Let $U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be an additive exact equivalence with inverse $V$. The inverse is additive because its Hom maps invert additive bijections. It preserves finite limits and colimits: applying the equivalence identifies the cone Hom universal-property bijections with those of the original cone. Hence $V$ is exact. For an acyclic $M'$ and K-injective $I$, the homotopy adjunction for $V\dashv U$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A')}(M',UI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(VM',I)=0$, since exactness makes $VM'$ acyclic. Thus $U$ preserves K-injectivity; interchanging $U,V$ (using $U\dashv V$) proves reflection, since $VUI\cong I$ as complexes and K-injectivity is invariant under isomorphism of complexes. Exactness carries a resolution quasi-isomorphism $a:N\to I$ to a quasi-isomorphism $Ua:UN\to UI$ with $UI$ K-injective, so $U$ transports K-injective resolutions. No preservation of K-injectives by $E_i$ is used anywhere.

proof.text: Agreement under equivalences. Let $U_0,U_1,W$ be additive exact equivalences $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_i'$, $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$, and let data $H',E_0',E_1',c'$ as in the statement be given on $\mathcal A_0',\mathcal A_1',\mathcal B'$ with natural isomorphisms $\alpha:H'U_1\cong U_0H$ and $\epsilon_i:E_i'U_i\cong WE_i$ such that $\epsilon_1\circ c'U_1=Wc\circ\epsilon_0H\circ E_0'\alpha$. Define $\bar\alpha:RH'\,D(U_1)\cong D(U_0)RH$ by $Q(\alpha_I)$ on K-injective $I$, using $\gamma'_{U_1I}$ (valid: $U_1I$ is K-injective by step 9), $\gamma_I$ and the exact-factorization comparisons, and extend it exactly as in steps 2-4 by the Hom bijection; likewise $\bar\epsilon_i:D(E_i')D(U_i)\cong D(W)D(E_i)$ is induced by $Q(\epsilon_{i})$ through the exact-factorization comparisons and the localization property of $Q$ for natural transformations. The two natural isomorphisms $\bar\epsilon_1\circ r_{c'}D(U_1)$ and $D(W)r_c\circ\bar\epsilon_0RH\circ D(E_0')\bar\alpha$ from $D(E_0')RH'D(U_1)$ to $D(W)D(E_1)$ are, at $QI$ for K-injective $I$ and after these identifications, $Q$ of the two sides of the assumed underived equation, hence equal there. Every object of $D(\mathcal A_1)$ is isomorphic to such a $QI$, so naturality and cancellation as in step 4 make them equal everywhere: the normalized comparisons correspond. The compositor $\kappa$ is treated identically with $Q(d_I)$. In the compositor transport assertion J need not preserve K-injectives. Extend the normalization equation for the H-transport square from K-injectives to every complex before applying it to JI: both sides are natural transformations into a functor factoring through Q, so naturality along a K-injective resolution and cancellation of its invertible derived image prove the equation on the original complex. Then substitute the two compositor normalizations and the J, H, and P transport-square equations; naturality and the given underived compatibility reduce the result degreewise to hd. Extend from QI to all derived objects by step 4.
